description:
Goal
Finish the native/codegen half of the shared runtime transport model at the omitted/direct-only seam: once runtime demand has settled that a callable never needs a first-class object, or that a delivered result carries zero lanes, native/codegen must consume that fact directly instead of re-deriving a broader runtime obligation.

Problem being fixed
fz-hwn.10, fz-hwn.11, and fz-hwn.12 moved the model upward: inputs, captures, returns, and delivered resumes now carry demand-shaped transport facts. Native/codegen still had two old-world assumptions left:
- a callable-producing step must either stay `DirectOnly` or be materialized immediately
- every native delivered return is either one scalar lane or tuple-field fast path

Those assumptions were wrong because layout had already answered both questions.

Solved seam
1. Native step lowering now has an omitted / never-materialize state.
- `BackendStep::FunctionRef` and `BackendStep::Lambda` bind structural callable values instead of forcing materialization at step time.
- Native only materializes a first-class callable object when some downstream layout actually asks for a runtime value lane.
- Absence from `ExecutableRuntimeDemand.callable_materializations` now means what it should mean: no runtime callable object should be created.

2. Native/codegen now have an explicit zero-lane delivered shape.
- `DeliveredShape` includes `Omitted`.
- continuation shaping, return emission, halt/writeback behavior, and callable-boundary adaptation consume that shape directly.
- Native no longer smuggles zero delivered lanes through an empty tuple-field path and then re-interprets them later.

3. Stale tests that encoded the old closure-object path are updated.
- Native tests now assert the settled transport contract:
  - direct-only closures may collapse to direct `Call` / `TailCall`
  - direct-only lambda sugars stay out of callable-boundary inventory when they never escape
  - direct callable identity can survive as executable activation identity rather than first-class callable-boundary inventory
  - structurally transported callable captures may contribute zero runtime lanes when the captured callable is itself zero-capture

Out of scope / follow-on bugs
The widened `compiler2_native_program_` and `compiler2_abi_ready_` runs still expose real remaining bugs, but they are not this seam:
- returned suspend continuation callable materialization has no settled boundary
- map fixture native/codegen raw ABI repr mismatch
- quicksort closure-capture runtime shape mismatch
Those are tracked separately after this ticket.

Design rule
- Semantic facts determine meaning.
- Settled runtime demand/layout determine representation.
- Native/codegen consume that representation contract.
- Downstream phases must not ask again whether an omitted value carries lanes or whether a callable should become a first-class object.

Code seams
- `src/compiler2/jobs/native.rs`
- `src/compiler2/native_codegen/demand.rs`
- `src/compiler2/native_codegen/terminator.rs`
- `src/compiler2/native_codegen/driver.rs`
- `src/compiler2/native_codegen/prim.rs`
- `src/compiler2/drive_test.rs`

Removal target
- Delete native step-time logic that re-derived callable materialization from lambda/function-ref syntax.
- Delete codegen assumptions that every native delivered return is either one value lane or tuple-field fast path.
- Delete stale tests that encoded the old closure-object path instead of the settled transport contract.

Checks
- `cargo check --all-targets`
- `cargo test compiler2_abi_ready_does_not_publish_unused_callable_constructors --lib`
- `cargo test compiler2_native_program_jit_runs_spawn_then_receive_through_compiler2_codegen --lib`
- `cargo test compiler2_native_program_routes_nontail_if_join_flow_through_continuation_entries --lib`
- `cargo test compiler2_native_program_jit_runs_source_lambda_sugars_through_compiler2_codegen --lib`
- `cargo test compiler2_native_program_marks_settled_singleton_closure_flows_with_exact_targets --lib`
- `cargo test compiler2_native_program_keeps_distinct_direct_callable_executables_for_same_surface_when_capture_identity_differs --lib`
- `cargo test compiler2_abi_ready_matches_direct_callable_captures_by_canonical_activation_key --lib`

comments.text: Current seam after mirroring demand-shaped local values into native executable inputs and entry captures: native direct-only callable transport still collapses at DeliveredResume because ReturnAbi can only express Value or TupleFields. Repro: compiler2_native_program_jit_runs_enum_reduce_through_compiler2_codegen fails in LowerNativeProgram with 'native call arg 7 for callee 66 expected direct-callable 65 with 0 capture(s), observed Some(Runtime(Var(7)))'. This indicates a direct-only callable returning through a continuation resume boundary and being rebound as a runtime value. Next correct step is to generalize internal return/resume transport from ReturnAbi::{Value,TupleFields} to the same value-layout model used for runtime params/captures, then thread that through artifact planning, backend interpreter DeliveredResume binding, native entry signatures, delivered_args_for_abi, and NativeDemandAbi/codegen delivered-shape handling. Do not restore old closure materialization to satisfy the test.

title: Compiler2 native: lower direct callable demand without first-class closure materialization
